title: Asking every day
literal_meaning: For the person who asks every day, there is no giver.
explanation: The daily asking meets an absolute “no giver” in the answering half. The dictionary defines the daily asker; it does not explain why help is needed or absent. Our reading considers the impatience that repetition can provoke, while questioning whether repeated need makes someone undeserving. Deliberate refusal is a possible interpretation, not an action established by the wording.
meaning_odia: ପ୍ରତିଦିନ ମାଗିବାର ଉତ୍ତରରେ କଥାଟି ଦେବାଲୋକର ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଅଭାବ ରଖେ। ଅଭିଧାନ ନିତି ମାଗିବାକୁ ଆସୁଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିକୁ ବୁଝାଏ; ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ବା ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ନ ମିଳିବାର କାରଣ ଦିଏନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ବାରମ୍ବାର ଅନୁରୋଧରୁ ଜନ୍ମିପାରୁଥିବା ବିରକ୍ତିକୁ ବିଚାର କରେ। ପୁଣି ମାଗିଲେ ବୋଲି କେହି ସାହାଯ୍ୟର ଅଯୋଗ୍ୟ ହୁଏ କି? ଜାଣିଶୁଣି ମନା କରିବା ଏକ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପଢ଼ା, ଶବ୍ଦରୁ ସ୍ଥିର ହୋଇଥିବା କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: Daily asking meets no giver; our reading considers impatience without assuming its cause.
odia_summary: ନିତି ମାଗିଲେ ଦେବାଲୋକ ନାହିଁ; ତାହାର କାରଣ ନ ଧରି ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ବିରକ୍ତିକୁ ବିଚାର କରେ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: A neighbour repeatedly borrows a chair for evening lessons. Someone quotes the saying in irritation. Another asks whether they could agree on a regular arrangement instead. The invented reply questions the refusal; it does not establish a traditional answer.
cultural_context: The source names no class or community. Its categorical wording is not evidence that people in continuing need are unworthy or that assistance is always refused.
